name: Spanakopita-Inspired Kale, Leek & Feta Frittata with Greek Salad (Prep-Ahead)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe utilizes 4 medium and 4 small food storage containers.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 bunch kale
1 small bunch fresh dill
1 English cucumber
1 pint grape tomatoes

instructions.primary_message: Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) pieces. Place in a medium bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl with the kale and set aside.
Preheat a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat.

While the skillet heats up, trim off root end and dark green top of the leeks, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut leeks in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add leeks and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned, 3-4 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, place eggs in another medium bowl. Add half of the feta, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine. Set aside. (Reserve remaining feta for the salad.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.

When the leeks are tender, add kale and dill to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the greens to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the kale is fully wilted, 2-3 minutes more. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

When the kale is wilted, pour the egg mixture into the skillet. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but top is still runny, about 5 minutes.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until top of the frittata is just set, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool completely, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, and spices in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
4 tsp red wine vinegar
¼ tsp oregano, dried
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve grape tomatoes and olives. Add both to the bowl and stir to combine the salad. Divide salad between the small containers, sprinkle with reserved feta, and set aside.

Cut cooled frittata into wedges and divide between the medium containers. Cover containers and refrigerate until ready to eat. Enjoy frittata at room temperature or warmed in an oven or microwave, with salad on the side.
